Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus-withdrawal ATAC/CUT&Tag time course
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with TPA, injury, or inflammatory signal), then remove the stimulus and track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding, chromatin accessibility, and H3K27ac at AP-1 motif sites over days to weeks. Persistent accessibility after AP-1 levels return to baseline would mark sites with memory. Like the 'mesh' and 'sync' in the material, the question is whether the sites stay linked after the driving signal stops.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming (degron/dominant-negative)
ideas.description: Prime cells, then use an inducible degron (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during priming or only during the later memory phase. Compare the secondary response (transcription, accessibility) to see whether AP-1 is needed to establish memory, to maintain it, or both. Like a 'rebuoy' that holds a state afloat, maintenance would be shown if removing AP-1 later erases the memory.

ideas.title: Primed versus naive re-stimulation with single-cell multiome
ideas.description: Run single-cell RNA and ATAC on naive cells, primed cells after rest, and re-stimulated primed cells. Test whether the memory state is a stable subpopulation and whether faster, stronger induction of target genes correlates with prior AP-1 motif accessibility. Quantify heterogeneity and the fraction of cells that remember.

ideas.title: Motif and site-specific causal perturbation
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or deletion of AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, or dCas9-based tethering of AP-1 or chromatin remodelers, and measure the effect on retained accessibility and on the recall response. Compare with control enhancers that are accessible but lack AP-1 motifs. This tests whether AP-1 binding at a specific site is sufficient and necessary for memory, not just correlated with it.

ideas.title: Lineage tracing and cell-division persistence
ideas.description: Mark primed cells (e.g., with a FOS-driven Cre or reporter) and follow their progeny through divisions in vivo or in organoids. Measure whether accessibility, AP-1 occupancy, and enhanced responses are inherited over generations, and whether they are lost on a predicted schedule. Pair with live-cell imaging of AP-1 reporters to separate a self-sustaining feedback loop (e.g., FOS/JUN autoregulation) from a chromatin-based memory.
